name: United Kingdom
summary: Three national MNOs since the Vodafone–Three merger (VodafoneThree, 31 May 2025): EE (BT), O2 (Virgin Media O2) and VodafoneThree. Merger remedies moved 78.8 MHz from Vodafone to O2 in stages (2025–2031); Ofcom's 2025 mmWave auction gave each MNO 800 MHz at 26 GHz and 1 GHz at 40 GHz.

operators.name: EE
operators.notes: Formed 2010 from Orange UK + T-Mobile UK; owned by BT Group since 2016. Also carries the Emergency Services Network (ESN) RAN.

operators.name: O2
operators.notes: Virgin Media O2 JV (Liberty Global/Telefónica) since June 2021. Acquired 78.8 MHz from Vodafone (VodafoneThree) for £343m as part of the VodafoneThree merger package (announced 30 Jun 2025; Ofcom consent 3 Jul 2025): 20 MHz 1400 SDL, 2×9.4 MHz 2100, 20 MHz 2.6 GHz TDD, 20 MHz 3.4 GHz, transferred in stages 2025–2031 (concurrent then outright transfers).

operators.name: VodafoneThree
operators.legal: Vodafone Limited / Hutchison 3G UK Limited / UK Broadband Limited (VodafoneThree Holdings)
operators.notes: Merger of Vodafone UK and Three UK completed 31 May 2025 (initially Vodafone 51% / CK Hutchison 49%). Vodafone bought out CK Hutchison's 49% for £4.3bn, completed 30 Jul 2026, and now owns 100%.

operators.name: Shared Access

notes: Ofcom's website (ofcom.org.uk incl. licence PDFs and the spectrum-trades page) returned HTTP 403 (bot protection) throughout this check. Ofcom licence URLs are kept from the davwheat seed; edges were cross-checked against pedroc.co.uk (Sep 2026) and trade press. Where only davwheat and one other non-regulator source agree, 'verified' reflects two-source agreement.

VodafoneThree → O2 transfer (£343m, 78.8 MHz): 1452–1472 MHz (concurrent 1 Aug 2025 – 30 Sep 2027, then outright), 2.1 GHz (retune Nov 2025; 2130.3–2139.7 MHz concurrent until 30 Sep 2031), 2570–2595 MHz TDD (concurrent from 1 Aug 2025, outright 30 Sep 2026), 3520–3540 MHz (from 2026). Concurrently held blocks are counted for O2, which uses them. Ofcom consented on 3 Jul 2025.
The 2.1 GHz '18.8 MHz' in the VMO2 announcement is O2's net gain counted both directions (2×9.4 MHz).
26/40 GHz licences cover High Density Areas only (68 towns and cities); outside them the same frequencies are available through shared access.
Upper 1.4 GHz (1492–1517 MHz): single 25 MHz SDL lot auction scheduled for Jan–Feb 2027; no use before 11 Jun 2027.
Unpaired 2100 MHz (1899.9–1920 MHz) licences are removed from the MNO licences from 3 Apr 2029 (Ofcom decision Mar 2024); then 1900–1910 FRMCS and 1910–1915 ESN gateways.
Totals include Shared Access (SAL) blocks under the 'Shared Access' pseudo-operator; these are not MNO holdings.
